title: Identification and customer trust
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Confirm the address, booking and authorised contact before requesting entry to premises.
Use approved identification and introductions when entering a customer's premises.
Refuse to disclose another client's identity, share keys or access codes, and escalate an identity challenge to the supervisor.

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Overview
instruction.body: This lesson develops practical competence in identification and customer trust for routine professional cleaning work. Apply the employer’s site procedures and stop if a task falls outside your training or authority.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body: Use approved identification, respectful introductions, privacy-aware communications and clear site access procedures.

instruction.heading: Prepare and verify
instruction.body: Use approved identification and introductions so customers know who is entering their premises. Confirm the correct address, booking and authorised contact before requesting entry.

instruction.heading: Perform the work safely and professionally
instruction.body: Never disclose another client’s identity, share keys or access codes, or allow an unapproved person to accompany you onto a site. Keep work communications within approved channels.

instruction.heading: Check, record and escalate
instruction.body: If a customer challenges your identity, remain outside restricted areas, provide approved verification and contact the supervisor. Do not pressure the customer to grant access.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

procedure: Confirm the correct address, booking and authorised contact before you request entry.
Use approved identification and a respectful introduction when you enter the customer's premises.
Keep work communications within the approved channels.
Do not allow an unapproved person to accompany you onto a site.
Never disclose another client's identity, and never share keys or access codes.
If a customer challenges your identity, remain outside restricted areas, provide the approved verification and contact your supervisor.
Do not pressure the customer to grant access.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

qualityStandard: The correct address, booking and authorised contact are confirmed before entry is requested.
Approved identification and an introduction are used on entry.
No unapproved person accompanies the cleaner onto a site, and keys and access codes are not shared.
An identity challenge is met with approved verification, the cleaner stays out of restricted areas, and the supervisor is contacted without pressuring the customer.
summary: The address, booking and authorised contact are confirmed before entry is requested.
Approved identification and respectful introductions let customers know who is entering their premises.
Another client's identity, keys and access codes are never disclosed, and an identity challenge goes to the supervisor.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do when a customer refuses entry or challenges your access?
options: Let an unapproved person come with you to speed up the visit
Pressure the customer to grant access quickly
Hand over the keys to the customer to end the discussion
Stay outside restricted areas and contact your supervisor

knowledgeChecks.question: How should access details be passed to the next worker?
options: Share the key code in a group chat so the next worker can get in today
Tell the next worker the code aloud in a public place at the front door of the building
Pass access details only through the approved channel, and not to unapproved people
Leave the key with a neighbour and tell them the access code and the address

knowledgeChecks.question: How should you gain entry to a customer's premises?
options: Confirm the correct address, booking and authorised contact, and show approved identification before entry
Ask a neighbour to vouch for you and let them see the job sheet and sign it for the day
Use any ID card that looks official and then go in through the back door quietly when no one is looking
Enter as soon as you arrive, to keep to time and then tell the client about the visit later

knowledgeChecks.question: Which practice at a customer's premises is unsafe?
options: Using approved identification at the door
Keeping work communications in approved channels
Confirming the booking before requesting entry
Allowing an unapproved person to accompany you onto a site

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do when a customer challenges your identity?
options: Give the approved verification and contact the supervisor about the challenge
Post the customer's name in a personal chat to ask a friend about it
Argue the point until the customer gives in and then leave the job unfinished
Leave without telling anyone and say nothing to the supervisor or the office
